subtopics.title: Two Records, Two Kinds of Error

questions.question: The Debtors Control account and the list of debtors are built from:
options: Journal column totals (control) and the personal accounts posted daily (list)
The same postings, copied twice
The trial balance and the bank statement
The personal accounts (control) and journal totals (list)

questions.question: A journal column undercast corrupts:
options: The list only, because pages are posted daily
The control account only — the pages were posted from correct individual lines
Both records equally
Neither record

questions.question: An error made in the ORIGINAL journal line, before totalling:
options: Affects only the control account
Affects only the list
Flows into BOTH records and must be corrected in both
Cancels itself out at month end

questions.question: When control and list disagree, the correct starting attitude is:
options: Trust the control account and adjust the list toward it
Trust the list and adjust the control toward it
Split the difference between them
Trust neither — either record can carry the error; only the evidence decides

subtopics.title: A Worked Reconciliation — the Debtors Side

questions.question: The DJ sales column was undercast by R200. The treatment is:
options: Debit Debtors Control R200 — the totals' journey shorted control; the pages are right
Add R200 to the list
Credit Debtors Control R200
Correct both records by R100 each

questions.question: A bad debt of R140 was posted to the debtor's page but never to control. Control must be:
options: Debited R140
Credited R140 — it still carries a debt the pages have already written off
Left alone; the list must drop R140
Credited R280

questions.question: The invoice to T. Osman (R550) reached the journal and control but never his page. The fix:
options: Debit control R550
Credit control R550
Add R550 to Osman's balance on the LIST — the pages' journey is the one holed
Remove R550 from the list

questions.question: After all four corrections, control (from R7 440) and list (from R7 130) both end at:
options: R7 440 — the control was right all along
R7 130 — the list was right all along
R7 310 — the average of the two
R7 500 — a figure neither original record contained

subtopics.title: The Creditors Mirror and the Supplier's Statement

questions.question: The CPJ's creditors column was overcast by R90. The effect on Creditors Control was:
options: Too large a DEBIT — control's credit balance is understated by R90
Too large a credit — control is overstated
No effect; the CPJ never posts to control
The list was overstated by R90

questions.question: The correction for that overcast payments column is:
options: Debit Creditors Control R90
Deduct R90 from the creditors list
Credit Creditors Control R90 — reversing the excess debit restores the balance to R5 330
Credit Bank R90

questions.question: An invoice from B. Bell for R330 was never posted to her page. The treatment:
options: Credit control R330
Add R330 to the creditors LIST, bringing it to R5 330
Debit control R330
Ignore it until the supplier complains

questions.question: A supplier's monthly statement is reconciled against:
options: The trial balance
The Debtors Control account
The bank statement
That supplier's personal account in OUR books — differences explained by timing or error

subtopics.title: The Method, Compressed — and Why It Matters

questions.question: The classification question asked of EVERY finding is:
options: Where did the error physically happen — totals journey, pages journey, or original line?
How large is the error?
Who made the error?
Which month did the error occur in?

questions.question: If the two corrected statements do NOT end on the same figure:
options: Use the control figure for the trial balance
A finding was misclassified or an arithmetic slip made — re-examine before moving on
Average the two endings
Carry the difference to a suspense account permanently

questions.question: A difference divisible by nine suggests:
options: An unposted item
An amount on the wrong side
A transposition of digits somewhere in the records
A casting error of exactly R9

questions.question: Monthly reconciliation matters because:
options: It replaces the trial balance
It guarantees no errors will ever be made
It is required before any sale may be recorded
It catches inevitable errors while documents are fresh — internal control made routine

questions.question: The control line says R7 440; the pages say R7 130. The difference proves:
options: At least one error exists — but not WHERE it sits
The control account is wrong
The list is wrong
Exactly one error of R310 exists

questions.question: The detective's first discipline is:
options: Always trust the bigger number
Do not pick a favourite witness — either road can carry a pothole
Always trust the control account
Adjust whichever record is easier to change

questions.question: The case ends when:
options: One witness surrenders to the other
The difference is written off
BOTH stories, corrected independently, tell the same truth — the meeting point
The month is closed with a note about the difference

subtopics.title: Four Potholes, Each on Its Own Road

questions.question: The DJ column added up R200 short. Which road is holed?
options: The totals road — the line is R200 too small; patch the line up R200
The daily road — the pages missed it
Both roads equally
Neither — the money was never real

questions.question: The R140 write-off reached the customer's page but never the control totals, so:
options: The pages must say goodbye again
The line comes down R140 — it still thinks the money is coming
The list comes down R140
Both records drop R140

questions.question: Mrs Peters's page reads R530 for a R350 purchase — digits danced on the page only. The patch:
options: Line down R180
Line up R180
Pages down R180 — only her page exaggerates; the line was fed correct totals
Pages up R180

questions.question: After the patching, the truth of R7 500 appeared:
options: Because the control account was believed
Because the difference was split fairly
In the original list all along
Where the two independently corrected records MET — a number neither original answer contained

questions.question: The reconciliation must end in ONE number because:
options: The business acts on it tomorrow — trial balance, statements, credit decisions
Two numbers take too long to write
The auditor only reads one line
The bank requires a single figure by law

questions.question: The quiet lesson under the loud one: monthly reconciliation gives mistakes:
options: No chance of ever happening
A one-month lifespan — caught by routine, not by luck or complaint
A one-year lifespan until the audit
A permanent home in a suspense account

questions.question: On the creditors mirror, the safe working habit is:
options: Copy each debtors fix across to save time
Skip the creditors side; it always matches
Re-derive every correction's direction from the mirror's point of view — never transplant
Adjust only the list, since suppliers keep the control

questions.question: The supplier's statement arriving each month is best described as:
options: A replacement for our creditors list
A bill that must be paid in full immediately
Proof that our books are wrong
A third, outside-built record of the relationship, compared item by item against our pages
